findings.title: load('sotus') returns a broken sklearn Pipeline instead of the documented SOTU speeches (Drive id duplicated with nips_model)
findings.description: EXAMPLE_DATA in hypertools/io/load.py assigns the SAME Google Drive id '1J0MBhpRwdT2WChfWJ4HXYq6jU4XpyJPm' to both 'sotus' (line 24) and 'nips_model' (line 27); the cached files are byte-identical (sha256 4f93308a...). That file unpickles to a CountVectorizer->LatentDirichletAllocation Pipeline, so hyp.load('sotus') returns a topic MODEL, while the load() docstring promises 'sotus is a collection of State of the Union speeches from 1989-2018'. Because 'sotus' does not end with '_model', load() also skips the model branch and returns the Pipeline through the generic path. Worse, merely displaying the result (e.g. evaluating it in Jupyter) raises AttributeError because the sklearn-1.0.2-pickled Pipeline is incompatible with sklearn 1.8's repr/get_params (see -002). examples/plot_sotus.py already contains the workaround comment "Note: 'sotus' loads a text processing model, not the actual SOTU speeches" -- i.e. the example was adapted to the bug rather than the data mapping being fixed. One of the two ids is wrong; the true sotus text corpus is currently unreachable through hyp.load.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import hypertools as hyp
d = hyp.load('sotus')
print(type(d))          # <class 'sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline'>
print(repr(d))          # AttributeError
"
findings.expected: A collection of State of the Union speeches (text data, per the load() docstring), or at minimum an object of a data type (list/DataFrame/array)
findings.actual: type(d) == <class 'sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline'>; repr(d) raises: AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'. shasum: sotus == nips_model == 4f93308a48002730866659bda7ef393f5451dc8360b9e3c91c9cf5d77f73a762

findings.title: Hosted *_model pipelines are sklearn-1.0.2 pickles: InconsistentVersionWarning on load, repr()/display crashes with AttributeError under sklearn 1.8
findings.description: wiki_model, sotus_model, and nips_model (and the mis-mapped 'sotus') unpickle estimators pickled with scikit-learn 1.0.2 under the environment's scikit-learn 1.8.0. sklearn emits InconsistentVersionWarning ('This might lead to breaking code or invalid results') for CountVectorizer, LatentDirichletAllocation and Pipeline, and the reconstructed Pipeline lacks the newer 'transform_input' init attribute, so repr(model), model.get_params(), sklearn.base.clone(model), and plain display in a notebook all raise AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'. model.transform(['text']) happens to still run (returns a (1, 50) topic vector), but the docstring's claim that wiki_model 'can be used to transform text to topic vectors' is only partially honored: the first thing most users do -- evaluate `model` in a notebook cell -- crashes. The hosted model files should be re-pickled with a modern sklearn (or converted to a version-stable format).
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import hypertools as hyp
m = hyp.load('wiki_model')   # InconsistentVersionWarning x3
print(m.transform(['the quick brown fox']).shape)  # (1, 50) -- works
print(repr(m))               # AttributeError
"
findings.expected: A model object that loads without version warnings and supports the standard sklearn surface (repr/get_params/clone/transform)
findings.actual: sklearn/base.py:463: InconsistentVersionWarning: Trying to unpickle estimator CountVectorizer from version 1.0.2 when using version 1.8.0 ... ; repr(m) -> AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'; m.transform() -> (1, 50) OK

findings.title: load() docstring dataset descriptions wrong: spiral type, mushrooms type + 'mushroomm' typo, weights_avg derivation, wiki structure undescribed
findings.description: Measured against real loads: (a) 'spiral is numpy array containing data for a 3D spiral' -- actually a LIST of two (1000, 3) arrays (the pair used for the procrustes demo); (b) 'mushrooms is a numpy array comprised of features (columns)...' -- actually a pandas DataFrame of shape (8124, 22) (load() itself converts it via pd.DataFrame), and 'mushroomm' is a typo; (c) weights_avg is described twice, as 'the 2-array subject-averaged version' and as 'the dataset split in half and averaged into two groups', but its arrays are (100, 100) float64 while weights arrays are (300, 100) float32 -- averaging subjects preserves timepoints, so 100 vs 300 rows contradicts the described derivation; (d) 'wiki is a collection of wikipedia pages' -- actually a list holding ONE (3136, 1) object array of strings; the nesting is not described anywhere. Also cosmetic: the Parameters section lists normalize before reduce/ndims/align although the signature order is (reduce, ndims, align, normalize), which can mislead positional callers.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import hypertools as hyp
print(type(hyp.load('spiral')), len(hyp.load('spiral')))
print(type(hyp.load('mushrooms')), hyp.load('mushrooms').shape)
print([a.shape for a in hyp.load('weights_avg')], [a.shape for a in hyp.load('weights')][:1])
w = hyp.load('wiki'); print(type(w), len(w), w[0].shape, w[0].dtype)
"
findings.expected: Docstring descriptions match returned types/shapes: spiral 'list of two (1000, 3) arrays', mushrooms 'DataFrame', weights_avg description consistent with its (100, 100) arrays, wiki structure documented, 'mushroom' spelled correctly

findings.title: Non-string dataset arguments crash with cryptic low-level TypeErrors instead of a clear contract message
findings.description: load(123), load(None), load(3.14) raise TypeError('expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not int/NoneType/float') leaked from os.path.expandvars; load(b'weights') raises the os.fspath variant; load({'a': 1}) raises TypeError("unhashable type: 'dict'") from the EXAMPLE_DATA membership test. None of these mention hypertools.load or state that `dataset` must be a string, path, or list of strings. A one-line isinstance guard at the top of load() would make all five cases actionable.

findings.title: Cache-directory creation failures surface as raw OS errors with no hypertools guidance
findings.description: _load_example_data() calls DATA_DIR.mkdir() bare. If ~/hypertools_data exists as a regular FILE (e.g. created accidentally), every hosted-dataset load fails with an unwrapped FileExistsError naming the path but not explaining that hypertools needs it to be a directory or how to fix it (delete/rename the file). findings.title: Unknown-name error digest never lists the built-in dataset names and offers no near-miss suggestion; Drive-id-shaped typos trigger live network requests
findings.description: hyp.load('Weights') and hyp.load('weights ') (case/whitespace typos of a builtin) fail with the 'could not load ... Tried, in order' digest, which enumerates the six scikit-learn names but never mentions that built-in example datasets exist, what they are called, or that 'weights' is one edit away. Additionally, any unknown name of >= 25 [A-Za-z0-9_-] characters matches _DRIVE_ID_RE and is sent to Google Drive over the network before failing (observed: 'definitely_not_a_dataset_xyz' triggered a real HTTP GET answered 404), so typos can stall on slow networks. Suggested: include the EXAMPLE_DATA names (or a difflib.get_close_matches suggestion) in the digest.
findings.expected: Digest mentions built-in example dataset names and/or suggests: did you mean 'weights'?

HypertoolsIOError: could not load 'Weights'. Tried, in order:

  - seaborn dataset: not found via seaborn.get_dataset_names() ...
  - local file: not found at Weights  (no mention of builtin names; no suggestion)

findings.title: Invalid normalize= value surfaces as AssertionError (assert-based input validation) through load()
findings.description: hyp.load('spiral', normalize='bogus') raises AssertionError('scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.') from the normalize stage. Using assert for user-input validation is fragile (asserts are stripped under python -O) and AssertionError is the wrong exception type for bad argument values; peer stages raise ValueError (e.g. ndims: 'ValueError: ndims must be >= 1; got 0'). The message content itself is good. Root fix belongs in the normalize module, but it is user-visible through load()'s documented normalize kwarg.
findings.repro:
env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import hypertools as hyp
hyp.load('spiral', normalize='bogus')
"
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: infra: repo .venv contains a stale NON-editable hypertools snapshot that silently shadows the working tree when cwd is not the repo root
findings.description: infra finding (environment, not shipped code -- but it invalidates testing). `pip show hypertools` reports Location: .../.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages with no editable project location, and site-packages/hypertools/ is an old snapshot: diff -rq against the working tree shows ~30 differing modules, an outdated load() docstring ('weights is list of 2 numpy arrays... 18 subjects'), the pre-fix _load_legacy message ('To load legacy-format datasets, install the deepdish module'), missing sources.py 502-retry code, and missing plot/hyper_animation.py entirely. Any process started with cwd != /Users/jmanning/hypertools (scripts, notebooks, other auditors' scratch dirs) imports the STALE package; running from the repo root imports the tree (cwd shadows site-packages). During this audit the discrepancy produced materially different error messages for identical code until runs were pinned with PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools. Remedy: reinstall editable (pip install -e '.[dev]') so the venv matches the documented dev setup.

cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools, sys; print(sys.modules['hypertools'].__file__)"  # -> working tree
findings.expected: The venv resolves hypertools to the working tree regardless of cwd (editable install), so tests and audits exercise the release candidate
